title: Explicit tensorator for cocontinuous module-sheaf restriction
statement: For a continuous functor F:(C,J)→(D,K) between small sites, commutative coefficient sheaves R on D and S on C and an isomorphism c:F*R≅S, construct the tensorator tensorPushMap from the sheafified sectionwise scalar-restriction tensorator. If the canonical restriction/sheafification comparison is invertible for every R-module presheaf, tensorPushMap is invertible. The latter condition holds when F is cocontinuous. The tensorator sends sheafified pure tensors to pure tensors and is natural in both factors. The coefficient isomorphism gives the normalized rank-one unit comparison. The tensor and sheafification constructions are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

source.place: section-tensor-product (03EK), and section-sheafification (03CY); explicit module-sheafification comparison and sectionwise scalar restriction

proof.text: Transpose the restricted sheafification unit along the source sheafification adjunction. Its composite with that unit is the restricted target unit. Cocontinuity preserves local injectivity and local surjectivity, so the transpose is an isomorphism of sheaves.

Define tensorPushMap by the canonical tensor/sheafification isomorphism, sheafification of the presheaf scalar-restriction tensorator, the transpose just constructed, and the inverse target tensor/sheafification isomorphism. Tensor the semilinear identity equivalences associated to c to prove sectionwise invertibility of the presheaf tensorator. Functoriality of sheafification and composition prove tensorPushMap invertible.

Evaluate the unit equation on elementary tensors to get the normalized tensorator formula. Maps out of a sheaf tensor are determined on these tensors by the adjunction and tensor extensionality; this proves naturality. The coefficient isomorphism and its inverse define the rank-one unit equivalence sectionwise, with linearity from preservation of multiplication. All constructions also apply to the zero ring and empty sites.
